\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} As sequencing data and reference collections grow, from complete genomes to pangenomes, finding seeds, the exact matches between a query and a reference from which reads are mapped and genomes are aligned, has become a central step of sequence analysis. Many kinds of seeds are in use, from sampled k-mers such as minimizers to maximal exact matches, and each is computed by its own specialized tool, with its own index and output format. And as processors gain wider vector units and deeper memory hierarchies, the speed of seeding depends increasingly on how well an implementation uses each core.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present sporos, a library that computes all of these seeds exactly, designed around each core's vector units and memory parallelism. Its main idea is to count the occurrences of a MEM's string from the MEMs themselves: the string occurs in the reference once for each MEM whose query interval contains it, so frequency-capped MEMs require no index beyond the one that finds the MEMs. On one Intel Skylake-X core, sporos was 1.8--2.3$\times$ faster than simd-minimizers for minimizers and syncmers, 3.9$\times$ faster than minimap2 for seed lookups, 2.0--2.4$\times$ faster than copMEM2 for MEMs between the GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 chromosome 1, 4.2--43$\times$ faster than MUMmer4 for MEMs and MUMs with identical output, 121--176$\times$ faster than Mumemto at its closest settings for frequency-capped MEMs, and 4.8$\times$ faster than minibwa for SMEMs of short reads.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} sporos is free software under the MIT license, written in Mojo with C, Python and command-line interfaces, at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/sporos}.}
